heroHeadline: NASA ASSIGNS ARTEMIS II CREW TO NEW MISSION FOLLOWING HISTORIC MOON ORBIT
heroSubtitle: Sep 28: NASA has assigned the Artemis II crew — Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen — to a new mission following their historic lunar flyby in April 2026, when they became the first humans to orbit the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. Aug 14: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said he is "extremely confident" Artemis III will launch in 2027, detailing the mission's three-launch sequence: Blue Origin's New Glenn flies first carrying a Blue Moon Mark 2 test lander, followed by the SLS rocket with Orion, and then SpaceX's Starship Version 3 with a docking adapter. HARDWARE: SLS solid rocket booster nose cones arrived at Kennedy Space Center's VAB Aug 13; the Orion crew and service modules were joined July 30. SETBACK: Blue Origin traced its May 28 New Glenn static-fire explosion to a BE-4 engine oxygen valve; Blue Moon Mark 1 cargo lander slipped to Q1 2027. Artemis Accords stand at 70 signatory nations.
